content: Disulfiram should never be administered to a patient who is intoxicated with alcohol or without their explicit consent. Patients must abstain from alcohol for at least 12 hours before taking disulfiram. Even after discontinuing disulfiram, adverse reactions to alcohol may persist for up to two weeks. Disulfiram is prescribed to manage chronic alcoholism. It works by inducing unpleasant physical reactions when alcohol is consumed, even in small amounts. These reactions include facial flushing, headaches, nausea, vomiting, chest pain, weakness, blurred vision, mental confusion, sweating, choking, difficulty breathing, and anxiety. These symptoms typically begin approximately 10 minutes after alcohol enters the body and can last for an hour or longer. It is important to note that disulfiram is not a cure for alcoholism but serves as a deterrent to drinking. In some cases, disulfiram may be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for further details. Disulfiram is available in tablet form and is taken orally once daily. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as prescribed, without altering the dosage or frequency. If swallowing the tablets is difficult, they can be crushed and mixed with water, coffee, tea, milk, soft drinks, or fruit juice. Before starting disulfiram, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to disulfiram or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially amitriptyline, anticoagulants like warfarin, isoniazid, metronidazole, phenytoin, over-the-counter drugs containing alcohol, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of diabetes, thyroid disease, epilepsy, brain damage, or kidney or liver disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking disulfiram, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking disulfiram. Be aware that disulfiram may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving or operating machinery until you understand how the medication affects you. While taking disulfiram, avoid consuming any alcoholic beverages, including wine, beer, and medications containing alcohol (e.g., cough syrups). This restriction applies during the 12 hours before your first dose and for several weeks after discontinuing the medication. Additionally, avoid foods and beverages containing alcohol, such as sauces and vinegars. If you miss a dose of disulfiram, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Disulfiram may cause side effects. Minor side effects include skin rash, acne, mild headaches, drowsiness, fatigue, impotence, and a metallic or garlic-like taste in the mouth. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Severe side effects requiring immediate medical attention include extreme fatigue, weakness, lack of energy, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, yellowing of the skin or eyes, and dark urine. Store disulfiram in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as regular monitoring is necessary to evaluate your response to disulfiram. Carry an identification card indicating that you are taking disulfiram and providing emergency contact information for your doctor or healthcare provider. If you need assistance obtaining an identification card, consult your pharmacist or doctor. Avoid contact with or inhalation of fumes from products containing alcohol, such as paint, paint thinner, varnish, and shellac. Exercise caution when using alcohol-containing products like aftershave, cologne, or rubbing alcohol, as they may cause adverse reactions such as headaches, nausea, redness, or itching. Test these products on a small area of skin for 1-2 hours before use. If no adverse effects occur, the product can be used safely. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Disulfiram is marketed under the brand name Antabuse®.
